heroIntro: Tell us what the system is doing and where you are. It goes to an HVAC company that covers your part of Houston, and they come back with a next step.
intro: Most AC problems in Houston are not mystery failures. They are a condenser packed with cottonwood, a system that was undersized for a house that got an addition, a coil that froze because the filter had not been changed since spring. Somebody who works that street every day recognises it faster than a call center script does, which is the entire reason this site asks for your area before it sends your request anywhere.
whyRequest: Your request goes to a company that already works your area
You describe the symptom in your own words, no ticket number
The company calls you back with a next step, not a survey
Nothing costs you anything, the company pays for the referral
You are under no obligation to go ahead with the work

steps.d: What the system is doing, when it started, what you have already tried. Three lines is usually enough for a technician to know roughly where to look.
Your request goes to an HVAC company that covers your part of Houston, so the person coming out already knows the housing stock and the weather.
You get a person on the phone who can ask the questions a form cannot, and tell you what the options and the costs look like before anyone turns a wrench.
The quote and the work are between you and that company. There is nothing on this site that obliges you to accept either one.

faqs.q: Is it free to request AC service?
faqs.a: Yes, and it stays free. The HVAC company that takes your request pays a referral fee. That fee never gets passed to you, and nothing on this site charges you for anything.

faqs.q: Why do you need my address and not just my phone number?
faqs.a: Because AC work is local. A condenser in League City is in salt air, one in Katy is under an oak tree dropping cottonwood, one in Bellaire has been sitting on a small lot since the 1950s. The company that covers your area will recognise the situation faster, and you are more likely to get someone who has seen your exact problem before.

faqs.q: How quickly will someone contact me?
faqs.a: That depends on the company that receives your request and on how urgent the problem is. If your system has gone down in the middle of a July week, say so in the description, because that changes how it gets handled. We do not control or promise response times on behalf of the companies that receive requests.

faqs.q: Will I get a price before anyone comes out?
faqs.a: You should get a sense of cost before work begins, and you should ask for it. The cost depends on access, time of day, which part failed, and whether it is a repair or a replacement. Any company that will not talk about cost until the unit is already open should not be doing the job.

faqs.q: Are the companies you sending me to licensed?
faqs.a: We do not employ anyone and we do not do the work. You should always confirm a contractor's license with the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation before work starts, and you can ask the company to give you the license number on the phone. That check takes a minute and it is worth doing every time.

faqs.q: My unit is running but the house is still hot. What should I do?
faqs.a: Do not keep lowering the thermostat. If the indoor coil has frozen, dropping the setting makes it worse. Turn the system off at the thermostat and let the coil thaw for a few hours, then try one cycle. If it happens again within a day, something mechanical is going on and it needs to be looked at.

faqs.q: What if my area is not listed on this site?
faqs.a: Request anyway. The list on this site shows where requests are actively routed, and it is not the whole metro. If nobody covers your street, you will find out quickly and nothing is lost. If you are outside Greater Houston entirely, you are better off searching directly for a local company.
